newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on loan prepayment.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on loan prepayment.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed down 45 basis points at 23.40 percent on Wednesday following news that Mexico was to prepay $5 billion owing on an emergency loan agreement, traders said.
"The message is positive and certainly helped rates to fall, although the market was a little edgy over a peso that weakened in spite of the news," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso closed 0.4 of a centavo weaker at 7.8030/7.8080 per dollar.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed down 70 basis points at 24.30 percent.

At the same time as the money market opened, Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz announced Mexico will pay the U.S. Treasury $3.5 billion outstanding on an emergency loan made in February 1995, and an additional $1.5 billion to the International Monetary Fund.
Brokers agreed that the reduction in short-term foreign debt for Mexico improved outlook and interest among investors, but did not foresee any substantial falls in interest rates in the short term.
"There is room for rates to fall, but not much, maybe as far as 22.5 percent in January," one broker said.
For the sixth session in a row, Banco de Mexico drained surplus liquidity in the market through two auctions to purchase 1.362 billion pesos in liquidity.
Liquidity of 1.203 from prior purchases by the central bank was scheduled to flow back into the system on Thursday.
